fields.description: Master switch. When off, the kiosk never samples or records location.
fields.label: Enable Location Tracking

fields.description: Hold a Screen Wake Lock while clocked in and active so the screen stays on. On by default since v1.480.0 (decided 2026-09-17): a phone that sleeps in a pocket stops reporting, and the tracking gaps that produced cost more than the battery does.
fields.label: Keep Screen Awake While Active

fields.description: Record a new point only after the employee has moved at least this many meters from the last recorded point.
fields.label: Distance Filter (meters)

fields.description: Even when stationary, record a heartbeat point at least this often (seconds).
fields.label: Heartbeat Interval (seconds)

fields.description: Request high-accuracy GPS. More precise but significantly higher battery drain. Off by default.
fields.label: High Accuracy GPS

fields.description: Fixes whose reported accuracy is worse than this many meters are stored as Low Accuracy when "Keep Low-Accuracy Fixes" is on, and discarded otherwise (0 = accept all).
fields.label: Minimum Accuracy (meters)

fields.description: Maximum number of points sent per network request (also the server-side cap).
fields.label: Max Batch Size

fields.description: An interval still Open or Paused this many hours after it started is closed by the hourly sweeper (workforce/sweeper.py): end time = the pause time if paused, else the last location fix, else start + this limit. The employee and their supervisor are emailed and the interval is flagged Auto-closed so the hours get a second look.
fields.label: Auto-close After (hours)

fields.description: A stretch of a clock-in with no location fix longer than this many minutes is a tracking gap. Drives the interval's Tracking Health, the gap segments on the Location Timeline, and the stale badge on the live map.
fields.label: Tracking Gap (minutes)

fields.description: Store fixes worse than the minimum accuracy as Low Accuracy rows instead of rejecting them. They still prove the phone was reporting (so they count toward tracking coverage) and the timeline draws them hollow; they are excluded from distance and stop detection.
fields.label: Keep Low-Accuracy Fixes

fields.description: The accuracy (meters) the kiosk tries to reach for the clock-in / clock-out anchor fix before giving up and using the best fix it saw. Anchors are what the off-site check compares against the project site.
fields.label: Anchor Accuracy Target (meters)

fields.description: Show the technician an off-site sheet ("You're 3.2 km from the site. Clock in anyway?") when the clock-in fix is outside the project's geofence. The server flags the interval as off-site regardless of this setting; this only decides whether the person is asked.
fields.label: Warn When Clocking In Off-site

fields.description: Automatically delete location logs older than this many days (0 = keep forever). Runs daily. Keep-forever since v1.480.0 (decided 2026-09-17): the trail is the evidence behind a corrected timesheet, and a 90-day purge deleted it before the questions arrived.
fields.label: Retention (days)

fields.description: First day of the FLSA workweek used for the weekly overtime split on the payroll export.
fields.label: Workweek Starts On

fields.description: Hours in a workweek beyond which hours are overtime. There is no daily overtime rule (Utah).
fields.label: Overtime After (hours per week)

fields.description: Employer burden (payroll taxes, insurance, benefits) added on top of the hourly rate for job costing, used when an Employee Pay Rate row leaves its own Burden % blank. Costing only; never reaches the payroll provider.
fields.label: Default Burden %

fields.description: Send each supervisor a 06:45 digest of yesterday: hours per person, auto-closed intervals, tracking gaps, off-site clock-ins and pending time correction requests for their team. HR Managers get the whole company. Nobody gets an empty one.
fields.label: Send Supervisor Digest

fields.description: Master switch for the capture gate. ON: a technician cannot switch projects or clock out of an interval without either attaching a photo or recording a skip reason. Enforced SERVER-SIDE in api/time_kiosk.py — client-only validation on a field device is not enforcement, it is a suggestion. OFF (default): the photo table and the kiosk camera still work, nothing is required.
fields.label: Require a Photo per Job

fields.description: How many photos satisfy the gate. Photos still queued on the device (upload status Pending) COUNT — the requirement is that the job was photographed, not that a cellular upload succeeded while the technician was standing in a mechanical room.
fields.label: Minimum Photos per Interval

fields.description: Let a technician close an interval with no photo by giving a reason. Turning this OFF makes the gate a hard block with no escape hatch: a genuine case (customer refused permission, camera broken, nothing visible to photograph) then has no way through except calling the office. Leave ON unless leadership has decided otherwise.
fields.label: Allow Skipping

fields.description: Require text with a skip. An unexplained skip is a data point about the process rather than a failure by the technician, but a blank one tells you nothing at all.
fields.label: Skip Reason is Mandatory
Default Time Category
fields.description: Pre-selected when a technician starts a job, so the common case is one tap. A time category is REQUIRED to clock in as of v1.485.0, and this is what stops that being friction. The requirement is not bureaucracy: an interval with no activity type produces a Timesheet Detail row with no activity_type, and ERPNext refuses to SUBMIT such a Timesheet — naming a row index rather than the job. Left unset, the accountant discovers the problem on payroll day, days after the person who could have answered it in a second has gone home. Leave blank to force an explicit choice every time.
